title: The Dead Village
timelinePosition: Directly after Chapter 2's close: the party walks into Millhaven at the last of the light, at the supper hour, on the day after the arrest. Verifier timeline: B1-B4 run from last light into full dark; B5-B6 at night; B6a is the night hold; B7 at first light; B8-B11 in the early morning and on into the day's ride south. Chapter 4 opens two days later.
openLocation: Millhaven, first human village south of the Quel'Thalas borderlands
transport: Mounted approach on Thalassian horses; on foot during the village sweep
immediateObjective: Sweep Millhaven, learn what happened to its people, and decide whether the threat is moving toward Quel'Thalas.
constraints: Absolute limited third on Sylvanas; nothing she could not perceive or infer
Jaina stays 'the mage' in Sylvanas's narration for the whole chapter (partnership-arc marker); she does not grow warm, she just stops treating the read as optional
Open on silence and procedure, not another fight (Ch 2 closed on three violent or dread beats)
No confirmation that grain carries the sickness: the granary reads loudest and Jaina refuses to treat it as the answer
No proof of an organized cult behind it; dead moving north is a direction, not a command structure
The old carter reads as ordinary, useful and forgettable; Sylvanas builds no case around him or his farewell
The grain-seller mention is a weak, unresolved clue: heard once, not connected
Second read of Beat 9 is plant only; the prose must not explain it
Keep consistent with Ch 2 B11: the deer was wounded and still on its feet, not reanimated; the sickness is active in living flesh before death
Fatigue registers for both women after a ride with no sleep
Neral and the unnamed ranger leave the book's southbound party at Beat 8; the survivor girl never continues south
Lyriel's carter answer is warm and true and must not sound careless

Arrival is at last light, not midday (Ch2 prose: 'the last of the light', 'the hour for supper'). The outline's 'stopped in the middle of the day' and 'tools that should have been touched that morning' describe when the villagers' life stopped, not the hour the party arrives.

Elves cannot feel the contamination directly (memory: world/magic). Every 'wrongness' Sylvanas registers must come through the horses, the silence, the staff, the mage's words or the frost on the mage's hand. Her bare-palm reading belongs to ward-stones only.
The dead did not march up the stretch of road the party rode in on in Ch2. The north-northeast line leaves Millhaven another way and cuts toward the ward line, not the Pass gate (see B7).

Ch2 images are callbacks, not discoveries: the mill wheel, the race, the inn sign, no smoke and no dogs (crest and walk-in), and the bowls left on the table (the Ch2 farm, which Sylvanas got from Cyndia's report).
The unnamed escort ranger is 'the fourth ranger' in Ch2 prose and memory. Their gender is not established, so keep them ungendered.

worldbuildingReferences: stories/the-plague-road/locations/lordaeron-and-northrend.md (border country, Millhaven: crossroads, mill, tavern, a few dozen lives)

povKnowsAtOpen: The contamination is real and big enough to matter beyond one village
Jaina's magical read is useful even when her sense of the physical road is weak
Millhaven is the first place on the south road where the wrongness knots tight
povDoesNotKnowAtOpen: How the sickness first got into the village
Whether the dead are moving with purpose
How large the threat is beyond Millhaven
mustNotBeImpliedYet: Any confirmation that grain carries the sickness
Any proof that an organized cult is behind it
Any hint that the old carter is anything but a useful local source
castKnowsLeavingChapter: Millhaven is the first village on this road fully taken
The survivor girl's testimony and the tracks confirm the dead marched north toward Quel'Thalas
Neral rides north with the survivor and the warning; only Sylvanas, Jaina, Cyndia and Lyriel continue south
A newer grain seller has been mentioned once, as a weak unresolved clue
Lyriel answered the carter's grain-seller question; on a first read it is nothing

pov: She opens treating this as a border problem to read and report, not a human disaster she has to carry herself.
The silent village and the missing bodies force her to read tracks, corpses, and magic together.
She starts the chapter using Jaina as a specialist, not a partner.
By the end, Sylvanas still does not trust Jaina, but she stops treating the mage's read as optional.

beats: Sylvanas expects Jaina to be good at magic and weak on the actual road.
Jaina proves more useful than that by helping separate the loudest wrongness from the real pattern.
Sylvanas does not grow warm, but she starts listening when Jaina speaks.

team.label: Partnership
beats: They begin as a custody escort with no trust between them.
Millhaven forces them to build one picture out of physical and magical evidence.
They do not soften. They just stop wasting time pretending the other half of the problem does not matter.

castAndHandoffRules: Cyndia: remains with the riding party. She is the ranger Sylvanas trusts most on the ground.
Lyriel: remains with the riding party. She talks to anyone on a road, and she is the one who answers the carter.
Neral: present at open. She rescues the survivor girl and rides north with the warning dispatch in this chapter.
Unnamed escort ranger: rides north with Neral and the survivor girl.
Survivor girl: found in a cellar. Escorted north by Neral. Does not continue south.
Old carter: helpful local source on the road. He should read ordinary, useful, and forgettable.
Next chapter starts: Chapter 4 opens after a two-day ride south with Sylvanas, Jaina, Cyndia, and Lyriel.

chapterBridge.previousChapterClose: Ch2 ends in Jaina's POV at the last of the light. From the crest Sylvanas orders 'Bows in hand. We walk them in. Cyndia, the left. Lyriel, the right. Mage, in the middle, and you stay there.' They go down at a walk, knee to knee between the garden walls; the hooves ring on the stone at the bottom of the hill; the inn sign creaks on its bracket at the crossroads. Jaina's last thought: was there anyone, one person, anywhere in all those houses?
chapterBridge.continuityOfState: Same moment, same formation, POV handed to Sylvanas. Neral is behind with the spare grey and the fourth ranger holds the rear. Both leads have gone without sleep since before the arrest; Jaina's right hand has been dead since the frost-sheet in the ambush, and she is sick with the old-coin taste. The doe, the ruled-line closure at Millhaven and 'Then I pick the ground' all happened yesterday.
chapterBridge.informationAsymmetry: This is the first time the reader has been inside Sylvanas since the Ch1 cell. She still holds the noon stone (late beat, cold under the warmth) and the circle on the map; Jaina does not know either. Jaina's question about whether anyone is alive was never spoken aloud, so Sylvanas does not know it. Her own reading of the ride (the culvert, the doe, the map) has only been seen from outside and is hers to carry in now without a recap.
chapterBridge.orientingAnchor: The crossroads at a walk, the inn sign and the ringing hooves, with the formation still around the mage. One callback is enough; don't re-survey the village from the crest.
chapterBridge.intentionalJump: POV switch only; no time skip.

scene.title: The Old Carter on the Road
scene.sceneFunction: Sylvanas sends the warning north, crosses paths with a casually helpful old carter, and commits her remaining force to riding south.
scene.knowledgeAtSceneStart: First light. The ground at the cut confirms the girl: at least sixty dead moved north-northeast toward the border. The survivor has to leave now with the dispatch, and Sylvanas has to weigh the border against the south.

beats.emotion: Tight, cold urgency: the theory has become a cellar, a child and sixty feet of ground, and she resents how much of this is now hers to carry.
beats.dilemma: Keep the full escort and risk the dispatch arriving late, or strip her own force to guarantee the warning and the child reach the border.
beats.decision: She sends Neral north with the girl, the dispatch and the extra escort, cutting her own strength to four for the ride south.
newOnPageInformation: Neral rides north with the survivor girl, the warning dispatch and the unnamed escort ranger
The southbound group is now Sylvanas, Jaina, Cyndia and Lyriel
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether the warning will reach Quel'Thalas in time
sensoryAnchors: dispatch tube strapped hard to Neral's saddle
beats.transitionIntent: action continuation: while Neral's horses are being loaded at the crossing, a wagon comes up the south road
beats.interiority: cutting her own strength for a human's warning, which stopped being a theory at the road cut; sending the child north or getting her off her hands; the Convocation will read the dispatch and argue the cost of the courier; three rangers and a prisoner, and the prisoner is the one who knows where to go
beats.timeAnchor: Early morning, straight after the cut.
beats.continuityNote: In Ch2 Neral was named the relay and planned to change horses at the Pass and keep going. She rides a bay and leads the spare grey ('fresh legs for the climb back'; the tooth-score on its near hock read clean), so the grey is the natural spare for the northbound pair. The outline's 'extra escort' is the one fourth ranger. Convocation: Ch1 left Lor'themar covering the budget session, and he has been off the page for two chapters. Sylvanas thinking about who will read the dispatch can touch that, and the interiority already does.
continuityCorrections: The outline interiority 'four riders and a prisoner' miscounts. After the split there are four riders in all: Sylvanas, Cyndia, Lyriel and the mage. Changed to 'three rangers and a prisoner'.
beats.plannerWarningResolved: 'Prisoner' as a status thought is fine; Jaina stays 'the mage' in narration (see constraints).

beats.goal: Learn what the road ahead looks like from the first ordinary local to come along it.
beats.conflict: The man is plain, helpful and sincere; his information is real but too normal to flag anything; he keeps looking past them toward Millhaven; his grain-man question is road gossip and Lyriel answers him as she answers anyone.

outcome.summary: They get a plain, useful read on the settlements south, still trading and alive, and Lyriel's friendly answer closes the exchange; nothing looks wrong, and that is the problem.

beats.valueShift: no source -> a source that is just ordinary
newOnPageInformation: An old carter with an empty wagon is shocked at Millhaven and describes the settlements south as still visibly trading
He asks whether they passed the young grain-man on the road
Lyriel answers: they passed no one, the girl spoke of a newer grain seller, they will watch for him going south; he would get a better price going home with a full wagon
Millhaven is the first village to fall; places farther south still look alive
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether any of his story connects to what really caused the sickness
sensoryAnchors: old grain dust in the wagon slats
surprise breaking across a forgettable face
his eyes going once along the line of horses
survivor girl leaning against Neral's saddle
beats.transitionIntent: dialogue hook: the exchange ends fast and the farewell is the only thing that sticks
beats.plannerWarning: Second read (plant only, prose must not explain it): he is checking his work and his agent, and Lyriel's friendly answer tells him the party has a witness and follows the grain-man south; he also notes how the riders hold formation and spacing. Plant these as observable behaviour only: his eyes on the line of horses, the spacing visible in the scene. No Sylvanas suspicion, no narration of intent. 'Grain-man' is the carter's phrase, 'newer grain seller' is the girl's; keep both without connecting them. Cyndia should be within earshot so Ch 9 and 15 corroboration works. Geography: he comes up the road from the south toward Millhaven (wheels roll north in B10) while the party leaves; do not have him turn back. Lyriel's answer should be worded by the writer; the voice sheet gives its shape.
beats.continuityNote: Cyndia must be within earshot (independent corroboration in Ch9 and Ch15). Keep the carter to a few short lines (malganis-voice). His eyes go past them to Millhaven and once along the horses: write the glance and never comment on it. For the plant, the southbound four should already be in their road order (Cyndia, Lyriel, the mage in the middle) when his eyes go along the line, so the spacing he sees is the one the Ch9 ward is laid to. Lyriel answers in her voice-sheet shape: warm, true, not careless.
beats.povNote: Sylvanas's agency here is the road: she wants the read on the settlements south and gets it. She has no suspicion, and the narration does not look twice at the carter.

beats.emotion: Mild, tired irritation at a pleasantry that snags for no reason she can name; relief at not having to think about it.
beats.dilemma: Whether the farewell means anything or is just road talk; she does not have the weight to spare to find out.
beats.decision: She marks it as odd, builds no case on it and lets the road separate the parties.
beats.valueShift: forgettable local -> a word that sticks for a second
newOnPageInformation: The carter's farewell, 'May the stars keep your road', lands strangely enough to stick
Neral and the girl leave the chapter; the party is formally split
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Why the farewell feels strange or whether it matters at all
sensoryAnchors: girl silent against Neral as the horse steps out
beats.transitionIntent: sensory carry: Sylvanas turns from the carter's wagon rolling north and faces the road south
beats.plannerWarning: The outline puts the farewell in the carter's mouth and Sylvanas marks it odd without a case. Do not let the narration say 'something about it nagged' for more than a beat; Cyndia hearing it too is the corroboration seed. The wording of the farewell is fixed by the outline and is not paraphrased.
beats.continuityNote: The farewell's wording is fixed. Lordaeron says 'Light keep you' or 'Safe road'; a blessing by the stars is the wrong note for a kingdom of the Light. Sylvanas marks it as odd and goes no further. No one replies with a road blessing (the Lyriel, Neral and Cyndia voice sheets all bar it). Neral and the fourth ranger leave here and do not come back.

beats.emotion: Duty satisfied on paper, with the odd discomfort of having put gaps in her own line.
beats.dilemma: Fall back to the border and let the Convocation own it, or keep following the pressure south into human land on a human mage's read.
beats.decision: She keeps riding south, and tells herself it is the trail she is following and not the mage.
newOnPageInformation: Sylvanas chooses to ride on south instead of falling back
The ride south is the next two days
The next village is alive enough to misunderstand what is happening to it
stillUnknownAfterBeat: How far the sickness has spread
sensoryAnchors: a thicker pressure from the front, read off the staff, the mage's face or the horses
two empty places in the horse line after Neral's departure
beats.transitionIntent: planted question: the next village is alive and has no idea; Chapter 4 opens two days into the ride
beats.interiority: the border is warned, so her duty is done by any measure the Convocation would sign; deeper into human land on a human mage's read; the empty places in the line, and she put them there; tells herself it is the trail she is following and not the mage
beats.plannerWarning: Outline B11 'still don't know grain is the specific carrier' is a hold-back note; the prose must not mention grain as a candidate carrier at all. Also 'the three remaining elves and Jaina' is the cast, stated for Ch 4's opening; do not narrate a time skip longer than the outline's 'two-day ride' close.
beats.timeAnchor: Morning, then on into the day's ride.
beats.continuityNote: Her arc lie is that the south is not her problem. Ch2 showed her acting on the truth without saying so, from outside; this is the first time she decides it from the inside. Elves cannot feel the contamination directly, so the 'thicker pressure' must reach her through the staff, the mage or the horses.

scene.timeAnchor: Early morning, then the ride south.

factsLocked: Millhaven is entirely dead, and physical tracks confirm its risen population marched right at Quel'Thalas

A survivor girl from a cellar was sent north
Neral carried the physical warning dispatch back to the border
The southbound party is stripped down to exactly Sylvanas, Jaina, Cyndia, and Lyriel
They've heard about a newer grain seller exactly once, but the connection hasn't been made yet
Lyriel answered the carter's question about the grain seller. On a first read it is nothing

Any explicit proof of an organized cult stringing this together
